tutorial.title: Discovering HTML and Tags
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn what HTML is and its importance in coding for the web.

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent:
Welcome! You're about to learn technologies like HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, and everything else we'll need to build for the web.

Before you realize it, we'll be creating real-life projects. Let's start with HTML.

lessons.title: HTML
lessons.interactiveContent:
Hypertext Markup Language, or HTML, is the computer language that structures the web pages on the internet.

On top of HTML, you can build stunning web pages and even powerful, full-featured web apps.

lessons.title: Creating a button
lessons.interactiveContent:
This is the code editor where we'll write code. Let’s jump in and start coding.

Click on <button>Like</button> to add the HTML code to create a button with the label Like.

Make sure to pick <button>Like</button>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
This is the code editor where we'll write code. Let’s jump in and start coding.

The HTML code <button>Like</button> creates a button with the label Like.

Build that same button by placing each part in order.

Make sure to pick <button>, followed by Like, and finally </button>.

lessons.title: Opening and closing tags
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's do this step by step. To create a button, first we need an opening <button> tag.

Make sure to pick <button>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To create a button, first we need an opening <button> tag. Choose the tag that starts the button.

Make sure to pick <button>.

lessons.title: Button label
lessons.interactiveContent:
The text between the opening and closing tags of a button becomes the button's label.

Add the text Like to the button.

Make sure to pick Like.

lessons.title: The browser
lessons.interactiveContent:
We already saw that the browser will show the result of our code. The browser renders our HTML code.

Rendering means reading the code and turning it into a page we can look at. Let’s complete the code to create a button to see it in action.

Make sure to pick </button>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We already saw that the browser will show the result of our code. The browser renders our HTML code.

Rendering means reading the code and turning it into a page we can look at. Finish the button with its matching closing tag.

Make sure to pick </button>.

lessons.title: Elements
lessons.interactiveContent:
Most tags come in pairs: an opening tag like <button> and a closing tag like </button>.

This whole thing is called an element.

lessons.title: Example
lessons.interactiveContent: Remember the previous example? In the next steps, we'll create the buttons for Q, R, and D. We'll ignore the rest of the code for now.

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
Time to create the first button.

Start with the opening tag <button>, then the content Q, and finally the closing tag </button>.

Make sure to pick <button>, followed by Q, and finally </button>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Create a button with the label Q. Use an opening tag and a matching closing tag.

Make sure to pick <button>, followed by Q, and finally </button>.

lessons.title: Lesson #15
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a button with the label R.

Make sure to pick <button>, followed by R, and finally </button>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Keep the first button labeled Q. Add a second button with the label R.

Make sure to pick Q, followed by <button>, R, and finally </button>.

lessons.title: Code a button
lessons.interactiveContent:
Finally, to complete this example, create a button with the label D.

If you complete this exercise, you'll also see the styled game using the three buttons you created.

Make sure to pick <button>, followed by D, and finally </button>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the example with a third button labeled D. Use matching opening and closing tags.

If you complete this exercise, you'll also see the styled game using the three buttons you created.

Make sure to pick <button>, followed by D, and finally </button>.

lessons.title: End
lessons.interactiveContent:
Awesome! We've learned how to create the structure of a button.

Soon, we'll also learn to use CSS and JavaScript to add styling and interactivity to our elements.

lessons.title: p tag
lessons.interactiveContent:
In HTML, the keywords of some tags are obvious, but there are some tags that use a shortened form. For example, we use p for a paragraph.

Which one of these HTML tags creates a paragraph?

<p><button>

Make sure to pick <p>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
In HTML, the keywords of some tags are obvious, but there are some tags that use a shortened form. For example, we use p for a paragraph.

Which opening tag creates a paragraph?

<p><paragraph><button>

Make sure to pick <p>.

lessons.title: Code a button
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's remember how to code a button. Code a button that has the text Post.

Make sure to pick <button>, followed by Post, and finally </button>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Let's remember how to code a button. Build a button that shows the text Post.

Make sure to pick <button>, followed by Post, and finally </button>.

lessons.title: Code a paragraph
lessons.interactiveContent:
Coding a paragraph is very similar to coding a button. You need an opening tag, followed by your text, and a closing tag.

Code a paragraph that displays Mimo is Fun!.

Make sure to pick <p>, followed by Mimo is Fun!, and finally </p>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Coding a paragraph is very similar to coding a button. You need an opening tag, followed by your text, and a closing tag.

In HTML, p is short for paragraph.

Now code a paragraph that displays Mimo is Fun!.

Make sure to pick <p>, followed by Mimo is Fun!, and finally </p>.

lessons.title: Code a paragraph 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code hello in between the opening and closing p tags.

Make sure to type hello.

lessons.title: h1 tag
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can create headings in HTML to emphasize certain texts. There are 6 sizes of heading in HTML, from h1 to h6.

Which one of these HTML tags creates a heading?

<h1><button><p><video>

Make sure to pick <h1>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can create headings in HTML to emphasize certain texts. There are 6 sizes of heading in HTML, from h1 to h6.

Which one of these HTML tags creates a heading?

<h1><h7><button><p>

Make sure to pick <h1>.

lessons.title: Code an h1 heading
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code a heading that displays SnapCat.

Make sure to pick <h1>, followed by SnapCat, and finally </h1>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use matching opening and closing tags to code a heading that displays SnapCat.

Make sure to pick <h1>, followed by SnapCat, and finally </h1>.

lessons.title: Code a button 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add the closing tag.

Make sure to pick </button>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the button labeled Accept with matching opening and closing tags.

Make sure to pick <button>, followed by </button>.

lessons.title: h6 tag
lessons.interactiveContent:
The heading tag emphasizes texts by making them bigger and bolder. h1 is the biggest and boldest and h6 is the smallest and least bold.

Which one of these HTML tags creates a smaller heading than <h1>?

<h6><button><video><p>

Make sure to pick <h6>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The heading tag emphasizes texts by making them bigger and bolder. h1 is the biggest and boldest and h6 is the smallest and least bold.

Which tag creates a smaller heading than <h1>?

<h6><h1><button><p>

Make sure to pick <h6>.

lessons.title: Code an h6 heading
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code a heading with opening and closing h6 tags.

Make sure to pick <h6>, followed by Little Things, and finally </h6>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Higher heading numbers make smaller headings: h1 is the biggest and h6 is the smallest.

Code the smallest heading so it shows Little Things, using an opening tag and a closing tag.

Make sure to pick <h6>, followed by Little Things, and finally </h6>.

lessons.title: Code an h1 heading 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the opening tag for the biggest heading.

Make sure to type <h1>.

lessons.title: Code an h2 heading
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the opening tag for the second biggest heading.

Make sure to pick <, followed by h2, and finally >.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Code the opening tag for the second biggest heading.

Make sure to pick <, followed by h2, and finally >.

lessons.title: Which is the smallest heading
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which one of these HTML tags creates the smallest heading?

<h6><h3><h4><h1>

Make sure to pick <h6>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You replace an h3 heading with the next smaller heading size. Which opening tag should you use?

<h4><h2><h3><h6>

Make sure to pick <h4>.
